html:
SMTO-HTTP-0013 — This connection belongs to a different task or Gateway

GUID: 65417441-78f3-4f5f-8a2d-3b7ce6b1fb80
Slug: http-connection-scope-mismatch
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO tried to use a web service connection made for another task, or on a different Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to reach other computers and services). The request was blocked and not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you changed the selected Gateway during this task, either switch back to the Gateway the task started on or ask SMTO to connect to the service again on the new one. Connections are tied to the Gateway they were made on, and SMTO clears the sign-in when the Gateway changes.
  2. In the conversation, ask SMTO to connect to the web service again and continue the task. A new connection is made for this task and the current Gateway, so it can be used.
  3. Before asking SMTO to repeat a step that changes something on the service, check on the service whether that change already happened. A blocked connection doesn't prove earlier changes failed, and repeating them could create duplicates.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects again and the next request shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume earlier changes on the service didn't happen just because this connection was refused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HttpConnections.resolve rejected a connection reference whose recipe belongs to another run or was bound to a different Gateway identity than the one now selected.

What this means

  • The connection recipe belongs to another run/Gateway, or its private runtime scope metadata fails validation. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The connection recipe belongs to another run/Gateway, or its private runtime scope metadata fails validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare run owner, exact Gateway identity and validated runtime scope; a matching hostname alone is insufficient.

How to fix it

  • HttpConnections.resolve raises this when recipe.run_id differs from the current owner, or when the recipe's Gateway identity differs from the resolved Gateway; in the Gateway case it also clears the run's HTTP auth via forget_run_auth. Call http.connect in the current run on the intended Gateway and use the new connection_ref; reconcile earlier writes before repeating them.
  • Create a connection within the owning run and target scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly established connection belongs to the current run and intended Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
